01 · UX strategy · Service design

Ration Seva

A government-ration service concept designed to make access more convenient, inclusive and transparent through doorstep ordering, scheduling and tracking.

Detailed case study ↗Figma source ↗
ROLEResearch · Strategy · UX · Product design
DURATIONApr–Sep 2025
CONTEXTIIT Delhi programme project
STATUSConcept proposal

Project Overview

The source study focuses on citizens who face long queues, time conflicts and accessibility barriers when visiting ration shops.

The proposed digital service lets people order, schedule and track government-ration deliveries from home while keeping transparency and fairness visible. It is a design concept, not a claim of a live government service.

Need for Design

Manual verification, physical queues and constrained opening hours create disproportionate effort for elderly and differently-abled citizens, daily-wage workers and families with limited daytime availability.

Design principle
Equity + convenience + trust.

Business Model

Three proposed mechanisms could support delivery and service maintenance; none represents confirmed revenue or an active partnership.

↗
Delivery

A proposed quick-delivery option to support last-mile fulfilment.

◎
Partnerships

Local farmers or merchants could extend access to additional grocery items.

◇
Funding and public–private support

CSR or PPP models could help maintain the technology and delivery system.

Target Audience

Designed for households with different access needs and daily routines.

⌂
Households

Low-to-middle income families using public distribution services.

Accessibility needs

Elderly or physically challenged citizens who face travel and carrying barriers.

◷
Time constraints

Working families and daily-wage earners with limited daytime availability.

Personas

The barriers below reflect experiences recorded in the supplied persona material; they are not presented as claims about every ration shop.

Persona A — Pocket Techie

Swaminathan

Age 65MaleBSc PhysicsRetired medical representativeChennai
Bio

Swaminathan is a retired medical representative whose son and daughter are well settled. He stays active through cycling, walking, and home workouts, and regularly takes his granddaughter to school. His day includes household chores, grocery shopping, using his phone, watching television, and spending time with friends in his apartment community.

Personality
CaringKindLoyal
Needs
  • Reliable wheat availability.
  • Affordable groceries and provisions.
  • Packaging that makes ration items easier to carry.
  • Scheduled collection slots to reduce waiting.
  • A responsive helpline for questions and complaints.
Barriers
  • Long queues can lead to unsuccessful visits.
  • Receiving change can be difficult, with pressure to purchase additional items instead.
  • Purchase notifications may show a higher quantity than the amount received, creating doubts about distribution.
  • Festival-benefit token systems can be unreliable.
  • Collection dates may be postponed even when a token specifies a date.
  • Access at other ration shops can be difficult despite the option to collect elsewhere.
  • Hurried packing can cause spills and product wastage.
  • Helpline complaints may receive no response.
Goals / Interest
  • Share his life experiences with his granddaughter.
  • Stay fit through exercise, cycling, and walking.
Tech Experience
  • Regularly uses UPI, WhatsApp, email, YouTube, and Instagram.
  • Shops for groceries through e-commerce platforms.
Design response

Surface stock and collection-date updates, support scheduled pickup, show accurate digital receipts, and provide a responsive help path.

Persona B — Offline Navigator

Sujatha Ranganathan

Age 55FemaleHigher secondary (+2)HomemakerChennai
Bio

Sujatha is widowed and usually lives alone, occasionally staying with her son or daughter. She follows a regular routine of cooking, cleaning, doing laundry, watching television, and caring for her plants. She enjoys preparing snacks for her grandchildren and growing vegetables and fruit to share with others.

Personality
CaringKindLoyal
Needs
  • More reliable wheat availability.
  • Ration-shop opening hours across the working week.
  • Easier access to eligible public benefits through a familiar service.
  • Assistance carrying ration items.
  • Better-quality essentials, including soap and tea powder.
Barriers
  • Missing products can require another visit.
  • She reports pressure to purchase additional items.
  • Purchase notifications may arrive for items she did not collect, reducing trust.
  • Failed fingerprint scans can delay collection.
  • Some products become unavailable after the first two weeks of the distribution cycle.
  • Unclear handling of outstanding change makes payments difficult to verify.
  • She perceives preferential stock allocation for people known to the seller.
  • Other ration shops may ask her to return the following week because stock is unavailable.
Goals / Interest
  • Prepare snacks for her grandchildren.
  • Grow vegetables and fruit to share with others.
Tech Experience
  • Uses a basic keypad phone rather than a smartphone.
  • Books LPG refills through a toll-free telephone service.
  • Can withdraw money from an ATM.
Design response

Show stock and benefit status in plain language, support assisted ordering and delivery, provide trustworthy purchase records, and avoid requiring a smartphone.

02 · IIM Trichy capstone · Agentic AI

GoNEX

Search Once. Book Anywhere. A proposed single interface for finding, comparing and booking everyday services.

AUTHORPraveen BG
ASSISTANTZiva
CONTEXTIIM Trichy capstone
STATUSProduct concept

Project Overview

GoNEX explores a single interface for finding, comparing and booking everyday services.

Users describe what they need in text or voice. A proposed network of specialised agents identifies relevant providers, compares options and helps the user confirm a booking. The concept brings discovery and decision-making together without claiming a live integration.

Problem and Opportunity

A simple booking can involve several apps, repeated information, and manual comparison. GoNEX explores one orchestration layer where users state an intent, review comparable options, and confirm a choice.

Ride app
Food app
Travel app

Repeat details
Compare manually
→
GoNEX

◉

03 · Product design · Industrial design

BitBox

A smart portable-storage concept with a built-in display for previewing, organising and managing files without a laptop or phone.

Detailed case study ↗
FOCUSPortable storage
INTERFACEBuilt-in display
DISCIPLINESResearch · UX · Industrial design
STATUSConcept proposal

Background

Portable drives hold increasingly large libraries, yet quick inspection and organisation usually depend on another device.

BitBox explores a portable-storage object with its own lightweight interface for direct browsing and essential file actions.

Current external-drive setups.

Problem Statement

How might portable storage support fast file checks and basic management without requiring a laptop or phone for every interaction?

Portable drive
→
Laptop or phone required
vs
BitBox direct interface

Desk Research

Host dependency

Conventional portable drives rely on a connected computer or phone to reveal and manage their contents.

Growing libraries

Larger collections increase the value of quick identification, folder navigation, and file status.

Action safeguards

On-device management requires clear feedback before destructive actions and after completion.

Market Research

BitBox sits between conventional portable SSDs, wireless storage, and media-backup devices. Its opportunity is not storage capacity alone, but making the contents understandable and manageable directly on the object.

Competitor Analysis

Portable SSDs

Compact, fast storage that typically depends on a host interface.

Wireless drives

Add remote access but commonly introduce companion-device and connection steps.

Backup devices

Prioritise transfer and protection rather than direct on-device organisation.

Design opportunity: combine portable storage with a focused interface for previewing, organising, and managing files at the point of use.

Goals

◉
Preview

Check a file quickly on the drive itself.

▦
Organise

Navigate folders and identify stored content.

⌘
Manage

Perform essential actions without connecting a second device.

Wireframes

High Fidelity UI

Technical Considerations

Performance and indexing

Fast local indexing with graceful handling of large libraries.

◫
Display and power

Readable states, responsible power draw, and clear battery communication.

▦
File handling

Format support, safe eject, data integrity, and clear reversible versus destructive actions.

◇
Security

Protected biometric handling with a secure fallback path.

Future Roadmap

Validate use cases

Confirm which direct-on-drive tasks create the most value.

Test interaction

Evaluate screen size, navigation, readability, and file safeguards.

Assess feasibility

Balance hardware cost, power needs, and the value of the added interface.
